import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Compute severity_score via PCA on (category, wind, -min)
sev = df[['category', 'wind', 'min']].copy()
sev['min_inv'] = -sev['min']
sev = sev[['category', 'wind', 'min_inv']]
sev_std = StandardScaler().fit_transform(sev)
pca = PCA(n_components=1, random_state=0)
df['severity_score'] = pca.fit_transform(sev_std).flatten()

# Log-transform damage outcomes
df['log_ndam'] = np.log(df['ndam'].fillna(0) + 1)
df['log_ndam15'] = np.log(df['ndam15'].fillna(0) + 1)

# Define formula and fit models
formula = 'outcome ~ masfem + severity_score + elapsedyrs'
models = {}
for outcome in ['log_ndam', 'log_ndam15']:
    df['outcome'] = df[outcome]
    model = ols(formula, data=df).fit()
    models[outcome] = model
    print(f"\nModel for {outcome}:")
    coef = model.params['masfem']
    pval = model.pvalues['masfem']
    print(f"Masfem coef = {coef:.4f}, p = {pval:.3f}")
    print(f"R-squared = {model.rsquared:.3f}")

# Residual diagnostics plots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
for i, outcome in enumerate(['log_ndam', 'log_ndam15']):
    model = models[outcome]
    fitted = model.fittedvalues
    resid = model.resid

    # Residuals vs Fitted
    ax = axes[i, 0]
    ax.scatter(fitted, resid, alpha=0.6)
    ax.axhline(0, color='red', linestyle='--')
    ax.set_title(f'Residuals vs Fitted ({outcome})')
    ax.set_xlabel('Fitted values')
    ax.set_ylabel('Residuals')

    # Q-Q plot
    ax = axes[i, 1]
    sm.qqplot(resid, line='45', ax=ax)
    ax.set_title(f'Q-Q Plot of Residuals ({outcome})')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from scipy import stats

# 1. Load data and filter missing values
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['alldeaths', 'masfem', 'wind', 'min', 'category'])
# High-intensity indicator
df['high_cat'] = (df['category'] >= 3).astype(int)

# 2. Standardize predictors in full sample
for col in ['masfem', 'wind', 'min']:
    mu, sd = df[col].mean(), df[col].std()
    df[f'{col}_z_full'] = (df[col] - mu) / sd

# 3a. Poisson regression on full sample
model_full = smf.glm(
    'alldeaths ~ masfem_z_full + wind_z_full + min_z_full',
    data=df,
    family=sm.families.Poisson()
).fit()
coef_full = model_full.params['masfem_z_full']
pval_full = model_full.pvalues['masfem_z_full']
print(f"Full sample: masfem_z coef = {coef_full:.3f}, p-value = {pval_full:.3f}")

# 3b. Subsample (category >=3)
df_high = df[df['category'] >= 3].copy()
# Standardize within subsample
df_high[['masfem_z', 'wind_z', 'min_z']] = (
    df_high[['masfem', 'wind', 'min']] - df_high[['masfem', 'wind', 'min']].mean()
) / df_high[['masfem', 'wind', 'min']].std()
model_high = smf.glm(
    'alldeaths ~ masfem_z + wind_z + min_z',
    data=df_high,
    family=sm.families.Poisson()
).fit()
coef_high = model_high.params['masfem_z']
pval_high = model_high.pvalues['masfem_z']
print(f"High-intensity: masfem_z coef = {coef_high:.3f}, p-value = {pval_high:.3f}")

# 4. Interaction model in full sample
# Use '*' to include main effects and interaction
model_int = smf.glm(
    'alldeaths ~ masfem_z_full * high_cat + wind_z_full + min_z_full',
    data=df,
    family=sm.families.Poisson()
).fit()
coef_int = model_int.params.get('masfem_z_full:high_cat', np.nan)
pval_int = model_int.pvalues.get('masfem_z_full:high_cat', np.nan)
print(f"Interaction coef (masfem_z_full × high_cat) = {coef_int:.3f}, p-value = {pval_int:.3f}")

# Wald test for interaction = 0
test = model_int.wald_test('masfem_z_full:high_cat = 0')
print(f"Wald test for interaction term: chi2 = {float(test.statistic):.2f}, p-value = {test.pvalue:.3f}")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.gam.api import GLMGam, BSplines
from scipy import stats

# 1. Load and preprocess data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['alldeaths', 'masfem', 'wind', 'min', 'category']).copy()
# Standardize predictors
def zscore(x): return (x - x.mean()) / x.std(ddof=1)
for col in ['masfem', 'wind', 'min', 'category']:
    df[f'{col}_z'] = zscore(df[col])

# 2. Prepare spline basis for masfem_z
df_spline = 6  # number of spline basis functions
degree = 3
x_spline = df[['masfem_z']].values
bs = BSplines(x_spline, df=[df_spline], degree=[degree])

# 3. Fit Poisson GAM with spline on masfem_z
gam = GLMGam.from_formula(
    'alldeaths ~ wind_z + min_z + category_z',
    data=df,
    smoother=bs,
    family=sm.families.Poisson()
)
gam_res = gam.fit()
print("GAM Summary:")
print(gam_res.summary())

# 4. Fit linear Poisson GLM for comparison
glm = smf.glm(
    formula='alldeaths ~ masfem_z + wind_z + min_z + category_z',
    data=df,
    family=sm.families.Poisson()
).fit()
print("\nLinear GLM Summary:")
print(glm.summary())

# 5. Likelihood-ratio test for nonlinearity
llf_gam = gam_res.llf
llf_glm = glm.llf
lr_stat = 2 * (llf_gam - llf_glm)
df_diff = df_spline - 1  # spline df minus linear term
p_value = stats.chi2.sf(lr_stat, df_diff)
print(f"\nLRT statistic = {lr_stat:.2f}, df = {df_diff}, p-value = {p_value:.3f}")

# 6. Plot smooth function of masfem_z
# Construct new grid
z_min, z_max = df['masfem_z'].min(), df['masfem_z'].max()
z_grid = np.linspace(z_min, z_max, 100)
basis_grid = bs.transform(z_grid[:, None])
# Extract smooth params and covariance
k_smooth = basis_grid.shape[1]
params = gam_res.params[-k_smooth:]
cov = gam_res.cov_params().iloc[-k_smooth:, -k_smooth:]
# Predict spline effect and CI
spline_pred = basis_grid @ params
se_pred = np.sqrt(np.sum(basis_grid @ cov * basis_grid, axis=1))
ci_upper = spline_pred + 1.96 * se_pred
ci_lower = spline_pred - 1.96 * se_pred

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(z_grid, spline_pred, color='blue', label='Estimated smooth')
plt.fill_between(z_grid, ci_lower, ci_upper, color='blue', alpha=0.3, label='95% CI')
# Also plot linear effect for reference
lin_coef = glm.params['masfem_z']
plt.plot(z_grid, lin_coef * z_grid, linestyle='--', color='red', label='Linear effect')
plt.xlabel('Standardized femininity (masfem_z)')
plt.ylabel('Partial log death rate')
plt.title('Spline Effect of Name Femininity on Hurricane Fatalities')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import math
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.manifold import TSNE
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Define functions for name-based features
def shannon_entropy(s):
    s = s.lower()
    freqs = {}
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha(): freqs[ch] = freqs.get(ch, 0) + 1
    total = sum(freqs.values())
    ent = -sum((count/total) * math.log2(count/total)
               for count in freqs.values() if total > 0)
    return ent

vowels = set('aeiou')

def vc_ratio(s):
    s = s.lower()
    v = sum(ch in vowels for ch in s if ch.isalpha())
    c = sum(ch.isalpha() and ch not in vowels for ch in s)
    return v / c if c > 0 else np.nan

# Compute textual features
df['name_length'] = df['name'].astype(str).apply(len)
df['vowel_to_consonant_ratio'] = df['name'].astype(str).apply(vc_ratio)
df['ends_with_vowel'] = df['name'].str[-1].str.lower().isin(vowels).astype(int)
df['letter_entropy'] = df['name'].astype(str).apply(shannon_entropy)

# Select and standardize features
features = ['name_length', 'vowel_to_consonant_ratio', 'ends_with_vowel',
            'letter_entropy', 'wind', 'min', 'category', 'elapsedyrs']
data = df.dropna(subset=features).copy()
X = data[features].values
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

# K-Means clustering into 4 groups (choose between 3-5 clusters)
k = 4
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42)
data['cluster'] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

# Cluster summary: average outcomes & female proportion
summary = data.groupby('cluster').agg(
    avg_alldeaths=('alldeaths', 'mean'),
    avg_ndam15=('ndam15', 'mean'),
    prop_female=('gender_mf', 'mean'),
    count=('cluster', 'size')
).reset_index()
print("Cluster summary:")
print(summary.to_string(index=False), "\n")

# ANOVA: alldeaths by cluster
groups_deaths = [grp['alldeaths'].values for _, grp in data.groupby('cluster')]
f_deaths, p_deaths = stats.f_oneway(*groups_deaths)
print(f"ANOVA alldeaths: F={f_deaths:.3f}, p={p_deaths:.3f}")

# ANOVA: ndam15 by cluster
groups_ndam = [grp['ndam15'].values for _, grp in data.groupby('cluster')]
f_ndam, p_ndam = stats.f_oneway(*groups_ndam)
print(f"ANOVA ndam15:    F={f_ndam:.3f}, p={p_ndam:.3f}")

# Chi-square test for gender_mf distribution across clusters
contingency = pd.crosstab(data['cluster'], data['gender_mf'])
chi2, p_gender, _, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(contingency)
print(f"Chi-square gender_mf: chi2={chi2:.3f}, p={p_gender:.3f}\n")

# 2D visualization via t-SNE
tsne = TSNE(n_components=2, random_state=42)
X_tsne = tsne.fit_transform(X_scaled)

plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
for cl in range(k):
    idx = data['cluster'] == cl
    plt.scatter(X_tsne[idx,0], X_tsne[idx,1], label=f'Cluster {cl}', alpha=0.7)
plt.legend(title='Cluster')
plt.title('t-SNE Projection of Hurricane Clusters')
plt.xlabel('t-SNE 1')
plt.ylabel('t-SNE 2')
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, norm
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# 1. Pearson correlation between masfem and masfem_mturk
mask = df[['masfem', 'masfem_mturk']].notnull().all(axis=1)
r, p = pearsonr(df.loc[mask, 'masfem'], df.loc[mask, 'masfem_mturk'])
print(f"Pearson correlation between masfem and masfem_mturk: r = {r:.3f}, p = {p:.3f}\n")

# 2. Bland-Altman plot
diffs = df['masfem'] - df['masfem_mturk']
means = df[['masfem', 'masfem_mturk']].mean(axis=1)
mean_diff = diffs.mean()
sd_diff = diffs.std(ddof=1)
loa_upper = mean_diff + 1.96 * sd_diff
loa_lower = mean_diff - 1.96 * sd_diff

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.scatter(means, diffs, alpha=0.7)
plt.axhline(mean_diff, color='gray', linestyle='--', label=f'Mean diff = {mean_diff:.2f}')
plt.axhline(loa_upper, color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'+1.96 SD = {loa_upper:.2f}')
plt.axhline(loa_lower, color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'-1.96 SD = {loa_lower:.2f}')
plt.xlabel('Mean of masfem & masfem_mturk')
plt.ylabel('Difference (masfem - masfem_mturk)')
plt.title('Bland-Altman Plot for Archival vs MTurk Rating')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# 3. Fit negative-binomial GLMs predicting alldeaths
formula_arch = 'alldeaths ~ masfem + category + wind + min + year'
formula_mt   = 'alldeaths ~ masfem_mturk + category + wind + min + year'
model_arch = smf.glm(formula_arch, data=df, family=sm.families.NegativeBinomial()).fit()
model_mt   = smf.glm(formula_mt, data=df, family=sm.families.NegativeBinomial()).fit()

print("Negative-Binomial Model with masfem (archival):")
print(model_arch.summary(), '\n')
print("Negative-Binomial Model with masfem_mturk (MTurk):")
print(model_mt.summary(), '\n')

# Compare AIC and log-likelihood
print(f"Archival model:   Log-Likelihood = {model_arch.llf:.2f}, AIC = {model_arch.aic:.2f}")
print(f"MTurk model:      Log-Likelihood = {model_mt.llf:.2f}, AIC = {model_mt.aic:.2f}\n")

# 4. Vuong's test for non-nested models (if loglikeobs available)
fam = model_arch.model.family
if hasattr(fam, 'loglikeobs'):
    llobs_arch = fam.loglikeobs(model_arch.model.endog,
                                model_arch.fittedvalues,
                                model_arch.scale)
    llobs_mt = fam.loglikeobs(model_mt.model.endog,
                              model_mt.fittedvalues,
                              model_mt.scale)
    diff = llobs_arch - llobs_mt
    n = len(diff)
    mean_diff = diff.mean()
    sd_diff = diff.std(ddof=1)
    vuong_z = np.sqrt(n) * mean_diff / sd_diff
    p_vuong = 2 * (1 - norm.cdf(abs(vuong_z)))
    print(f"Vuong test statistic = {vuong_z:.3f}, p-value = {p_vuong:.3f}")
    if vuong_z > 1.96:
        print("Archival model fits significantly better (Vuong test).")
    elif vuong_z < -1.96:
        print("MTurk model fits significantly better (Vuong test).")
    else:
        print("No significant difference in model fit (Vuong test).")
else:
    print("Vuong test not available: 'loglikeobs' method not implemented.")
    # Fallback interpretation by AIC
    better = 'archival' if model_arch.aic < model_mt.aic else 'MTurk'
    print(f"Based on AIC, the {better} rating provides better fit.")

except ImportError:
    install('pandas'); install('numpy'); install('statsmodels'); install('matplotlib')
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np
    import statsmodels.api as sm
    import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load and preprocess data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['alldeaths', 'masfem', 'category', 'wind', 'min', 'year']).copy()
# Standardize predictors
def zscore(x): return (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
df['masfem_z'] = zscore(df['masfem'])
df['category_z'] = zscore(df['category'])
df['wind_z']    = zscore(df['wind'])
df['min_z']     = zscore(df['min'])

# Structural break tests over candidate years
results = []
# Choose candidate break years allowing >=5 years before and after
years = sorted(df['year'].unique())
min_year, max_year = int(min(years)), int(max(years))
candidates = range(min_year + 5, max_year - 4)

for T in candidates:
    df['post'] = (df['year'] > T).astype(int)
    # Poisson regression with interaction term
    formula = 'alldeaths ~ masfem_z + category_z + wind_z + min_z + post + masfem_z:post'
    model = smf.glm(formula=formula, data=df, family=sm.families.Poisson()).fit()
    # Extract p-value for interaction
    term = 'masfem_z:post'
    pval = model.pvalues.get(term, np.nan)
    coef = model.params.get(term, np.nan)
    results.append({'break_year': T, 'coef_diff': coef, 'p_value': pval})

res_df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print("Structural break test results (interaction of masfem_z and post):")
print(res_df.to_string(index=False))

# Plot p-values across candidate break years
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.plot(res_df['break_year'], res_df['p_value'], marker='o', linestyle='-')
plt.axhline(0.05, color='red', linestyle='--', label='α = 0.05')
plt.xlabel('Candidate Break Year (T)')
plt.ylabel('P-value for Interaction Term')
plt.title('Structural Break Test: Femininity Effect Pre vs Post T')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Estimate the causal effect of being a female-gendered name (gender_mf=1) on fatalities by matching female and male storms on wind_z, min_z, category_z, and elapsedyrs.  
• Fit a logistic regression predicting gender_mf from covariates to obtain propensity scores.

import subprocess, sys

def install(pkg):
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', pkg])

# Imports

    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
    from scipy.stats import ttest_rel
except ImportError:
    install('pandas')
    install('numpy')
    install('scikit-learn')
    install('scipy')
    import pandas as pd
    import numpy as np
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
    from scipy.stats import ttest_rel

# 1. Load data and drop missing
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['gender_mf','wind','min','category','elapsedyrs','alldeaths']).copy()

# 2. Standardize covariates for propensity model
covs = ['wind','min','category','elapsedyrs']
scaler = StandardScaler()
df[[c + '_z' for c in covs]] = scaler.fit_transform(df[covs])

# 3. Fit logistic regression for propensity scores
treat = df['gender_mf'].values
X_ps = df[[c + '_z' for c in covs]].values
logreg = LogisticRegression(solver='lbfgs')
ps_model = logreg.fit(X_ps, treat)
df['pscore'] = ps_model.predict_proba(X_ps)[:,1]

# 4. Nearest-neighbor matching 1:1 without replacement
treated_idx = df.index[df['gender_mf']==1].tolist()
control_idx = df.index[df['gender_mf']==0].tolist()
ps_t = df.loc[treated_idx, 'pscore'].values.reshape(-1,1)
ps_c = df.loc[control_idx, 'pscore'].values.reshape(-1,1)
nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1).fit(ps_c)
dists, nbrs = nn.kneighbors(ps_t)
matched_controls = [control_idx[i[0]] for i in nbrs]
matched_treats = treated_idx.copy()

matched = pd.DataFrame({
    'treat_idx': matched_treats,
    'ctrl_idx': matched_controls
})
# 5. Assess covariate balance
def smd(a, b):
    return (a.mean() - b.mean()) / np.sqrt((a.std()**2 + b.std()**2) / 2)
print("Covariate balance before and after matching (SMD):")
balance = []
for c in covs:
    a_all = df.loc[treated_idx, c + '_z']
    b_all = df.loc[control_idx, c + '_z']
    smd_before = smd(a_all, b_all)
    a_mat = df.loc[matched_treats, c + '_z']
    b_mat = df.loc[matched_controls, c + '_z']
    smd_after = smd(a_mat, b_mat)
    balance.append((c, smd_before, smd_after))
balance_df = pd.DataFrame(balance, columns=['covariate','SMD_before','SMD_after'])
print(balance_df.to_string(index=False))

# 6. Compare outcomes and compute ATT
y_t = df.loc[matched_treats, 'alldeaths'].values
y_c = df.loc[matched_controls, 'alldeaths'].values
att = np.mean(y_t - y_c)
stat, pval = ttest_rel(y_t, y_c)
print(f"\nMatched sample size: {len(y_t)} pairs")
print(f"Mean alldeaths - treated: {y_t.mean():.2f}, control: {y_c.mean():.2f}")
print(f"ATT (treated minus control): {att:.2f}")
print(f"Paired t-test: t={stat:.3f}, p-value={pval:.3f}")

# Bootstrap CI for ATT
diffs = y_t - y_c
n_boot = 1000
boot_atts = []
for _ in range(n_boot):
    idx = np.random.choice(len(diffs), size=len(diffs), replace=True)
    boot_atts.append(np.mean(diffs[idx]))
ci_lower, ci_upper = np.percentile(boot_atts, [2.5, 97.5])
print(f"Bootstrap 95% CI for ATT: [{ci_lower:.2f}, {ci_upper:.2f}]")

Experiment Plan: Quantile Regression of Fatalities on Name Masculinity

Apply quantile regression (e.g. via `statsmodels`’ QuantReg) at the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles of alldeaths on predictors masfem, gender_mf, category, wind, min, ndam15, and elapsedyrs. Plot the masfem coefficient as a function of quantile to examine how the name‐fatality relationship differs for low‐lethality vs. high‐lethality storms. Include bootstrapped confidence intervals for each quantile estimate.
code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load and clean data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
vars_needed = ['alldeaths','masfem','gender_mf','category','wind','min','ndam15','elapsedyrs']
df = df.dropna(subset=vars_needed).copy()

# Create category dummies
df['category'] = df['category'].astype(int)
dummies = pd.get_dummies(df['category'], prefix='cat', drop_first=True)
df = pd.concat([df, dummies], axis=1)

# Define response and predictors
y = df['alldeaths']
predictors = ['masfem','gender_mf','wind','min','ndam15','elapsedyrs'] + list(dummies.columns)
X_df = sm.add_constant(df[predictors])

# Convert to numpy arrays of floats to avoid object dtype errors
y_arr = y.values.astype(float)
X_arr = X_df.values.astype(float)

# Quantiles to estimate
quantiles = [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]
results = {}

n = len(y_arr)
B = 200  # bootstrap samples
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

for q in quantiles:
    # Fit quantile regression
    mod = sm.QuantReg(y_arr, X_arr)
    res = mod.fit(q=q)
    coef_q = res.params[1]  # index 1 corresponds to 'masfem'

    # Bootstrap for CI
    boot_coefs = []
    for _ in range(B):
        idx = rng.integers(0, n, n)
        yb = y_arr[idx]
        Xb = X_arr[idx]
        try:
            resb = sm.QuantReg(yb, Xb).fit(q=q, max_iter=1000)
            boot_coefs.append(resb.params[1])
        except Exception:
            pass
    if len(boot_coefs) < B:
        print(f"Warning: {len(boot_coefs)} successful bootstraps for quantile={q}")
    ci_low, ci_high = np.percentile(boot_coefs, [2.5, 97.5])
    results[q] = {'coef': coef_q, 'ci_lower': ci_low, 'ci_upper': ci_high}

# Display results
tab = pd.DataFrame({q: [results[q]['coef'], results[q]['ci_lower'], results[q]['ci_upper']] for q in quantiles},
                   index=['coef','ci_lower','ci_upper']).T
print("Quantile regression estimates for masfem with 95% bootstrap CIs:")
print(tab)

# Plot coefficient vs quantile with CIs
qs = np.array(quantiles)
coefs = np.array([results[q]['coef'] for q in qs])
ci_l = np.array([results[q]['ci_lower'] for q in qs])
ci_u = np.array([results[q]['ci_upper'] for q in qs])

plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
plt.errorbar(qs, coefs, yerr=[coefs-ci_l, ci_u-coefs], fmt='o-', capsize=5)
plt.xlabel('Quantile (τ)')
plt.ylabel('Coefficient on masfem')
plt.title('Quantile Regression Coefficient on masfem')
plt.xticks(qs)
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

for k in ks:

    inertias.append(km.inertia_)
    sil_scores.append(silhouette_score(X_std, km.labels_))

# Plot elbow and silhouette

axes[1].set_ylabel('Silhouette Score')

df_nb = endog.size - len(nb_model.params)

var_resid = result.scale            # residual variance
icc = var_name / (var_name + var_resid)

# Print results

print(f"Random intercept variance (name): {var_name:.4f}")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import subprocess
import sys

def install(pkg):
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', pkg])

# Ensure LightGBM and SHAP are installed
try:
    import lightgbm as lgb
except ImportError:
    install('lightgbm')
    import lightgbm as lgb

try:
    import shap
except ImportError:
    install('shap')
    import shap

# Load and prepare data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
features = ['masfem', 'category', 'wind', 'min', 'elapsedyrs', 'year', 'gender_mf', 'ndam15']
df = df.dropna(subset=features + ['alldeaths'])
X = df[features]
y = df['alldeaths']

# Fit a light gradient boosting model with modest settings
model = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
    n_estimators=100,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    num_leaves=31,
    max_depth=5,
    random_state=42
)
model.fit(X, y)

# Compute SHAP values
explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X)

# Feature importance by mean absolute SHAP value
mean_abs_shap = np.mean(np.abs(shap_values), axis=0)
shap_importance = pd.DataFrame({
    'feature': features,
    'mean_abs_shap': mean_abs_shap
}).sort_values('mean_abs_shap', ascending=False)
print("Feature importance (by mean |SHAP|):")
print(shap_importance.to_string(index=False))

# Plot bar chart of SHAP importances
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.barh(shap_importance['feature'], shap_importance['mean_abs_shap'], color='steelblue')
plt.xlabel('Mean |SHAP value|')
plt.title('Feature importance from SHAP values')
plt.gca().invert_yaxis()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# SHAP dependence plot for masfem
shap.dependence_plot('masfem', shap_values, X, interaction_index=None)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Experiment Plan: Agreement and Reliability Between Archival and MTurk Femininity Ratings

Pair each masfem and masfem_mturk rating for the same storm. Compute the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) to assess absolute agreement. Generate a Bland–Altman plot by plotting the per‐storm difference (masfem_mturk–masfem) against the per‐storm mean ((masfem_mturk+masfem)/2), and compute the mean difference and limits of agreement (±1.96 SD). import subprocess
import sys

def install(package):
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', package])

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Import pingouin for ICC
try:
    import pingouin as pg
except ImportError:
    install('pingouin')
    import pingouin as pg

# Load data and drop missing ratings
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df2 = df[['masfem', 'masfem_mturk']].dropna().reset_index(drop=True)

# Prepare long format for ICC calculation
df_long = df2.reset_index().melt(id_vars=['index'], value_vars=['masfem', 'masfem_mturk'],
                                 var_name='rater', value_name='score')
# Rename index column to targets
df_long.rename(columns={'index': 'target'}, inplace=True)

# Compute ICC
icc_res = pg.intraclass_corr(data=df_long, targets='target', raters='rater', ratings='score')
# Select two-way random, absolute agreement single measure (ICC2)
icc2 = icc_res.loc[icc_res['Type'] == 'ICC2', 'ICC'].values
icc2k = icc_res.loc[icc_res['Type'] == 'ICC2k', 'ICC'].values
print(f"ICC2 (single measure, absolute agreement): {icc2[0]:.3f}")
print(f"ICC2k (average measure, absolute agreement): {icc2k[0]:.3f}\n")

# Compute differences and means for Bland-Altman
df2['diff'] = df2['masfem_mturk'] - df2['masfem']
df2['mean_rating'] = (df2['masfem_mturk'] + df2['masfem']) / 2
mean_diff = df2['diff'].mean()
sd_diff = df2['diff'].std(ddof=1)
loa_upper = mean_diff + 1.96 * sd_diff
loa_lower = mean_diff - 1.96 * sd_diff

print("Bland–Altman statistics:")
print(f"Mean difference (MTurk - Archival): {mean_diff:.3f}")
print(f"Limits of agreement: [{loa_lower:.3f}, {loa_upper:.3f}]\n")

# One-sample t-test for mean difference
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_1samp(df2['diff'], 0)
print(f"One-sample t-test on differences: t = {t_stat:.3f}, p = {p_val:.3f}\n")

# Plot Bland–Altman
to_plot = df2[['mean_rating', 'diff']]
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.scatter(to_plot['mean_rating'], to_plot['diff'], alpha=0.7)
plt.axhline(mean_diff, color='red', linestyle='--', label='Mean difference')
plt.axhline(loa_upper, color='grey', linestyle='--', label='+1.96 SD')
plt.axhline(loa_lower, color='grey', linestyle='--', label='-1.96 SD')
plt.xlabel('Mean of ratings')
plt.ylabel('Difference (MTurk - Archival)')
plt.title('Bland–Altman Plot for Femininity Ratings')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
